members.name: has_prefix
members.summary: Report whether the `runes` value starts with the element or run, or with any of a set of them.

doc.markdown:
The prefix/suffix tests take an element, a run, or a variadic run set — no predicate, no absent form ("first
symbol satisfies f" is `index(f) == 0`).

doc.code:
u"foobar".has_prefix("foo")             // => true
u"foobar".has_prefix('f')               // => true
u"foobar".has_prefix("bar", "foo")      // => true — set

members.name: has_suffix
members.summary: Report whether the `runes` value ends with the element or run, or with any of a set of them; see [`has_prefix`](kavun:type/runes/has_prefix).

members.name: index
members.summary: Answer the first position of a match of an element, a run or a predicate, or `undefined` (the `default` when given) on a miss.

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/runes#callbacks)).

The only two locators. Element, run, predicate, or absent; a miss answers `undefined` — never `-1` — or the
optional trailing default. Deliberately singular: `index` can miss, so its second argument is the default, and
there is no variadic set form.

doc.code:
u"héllo".index('l')             // => 2 — symbol position
u"héllo".index("llo")           // => 2
u"abc".index(func(r) { return r > 'a' })    // => 1
u"abc".index('z')               // => undefined
u"abc".index('z', -1)           // => -1 — only if you ask for it
u"héllo".index_last('l')        // => 3

members.name: index_last
members.summary: Answer the last position of a match, or `undefined` (the `default` when given) on a miss; see [`index`](kavun:type/runes/index).

members.name: insert
members.summary: Insert each argument as one element at position `i`.

doc.markdown:
`insert(i, ...items)` is `push` at a position; as a positional **edit**, `i` outside `[0, len]` raises (negative
`i` counts from the end).

doc.code:
u"ab".insert(1, 'x')                    // => u"axb"
u"ab".insert(3, 'x')                    // Error: index_out_of_bounds: (insert) 3 out of range [0, 2]

members.name: insert_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `insert`.

members.name: int
members.summary: Parse the text as an `int`; bad text raises unless a default is given.

doc.code:
u"42".int()             // => 42
u"4x".int()             // Error: conversion
u"4x".int(0)            // => 0

members.name: is_ascii
members.summary: Report whether every element is below `U+0080`.

members.name: is_empty
members.summary: Report whether the `runes` value has no elements.

doc.code: u"".is_empty()      // => true

members.name: is_true
members.summary: Report truthiness, which is non-emptiness: `!!x` ⟺ `x != runes()`.

members.name: is_valid
members.summary: Report whether every element is a real symbol, with no [octet escapes](kavun:type/string#undecodable-octets).

members.name: kebab_case
members.summary: Render the text as a `kebab-case` identifier; see [`snake_case`](kavun:type/runes/snake_case).

members.name: keep
members.summary: Keep only the matches of an element, a run, a set or a predicate; with no argument, the significant elements; see [`remove`](kavun:type/runes/remove).

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/runes#callbacks)).

members.name: keep_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `keep`.

members.name: last
members.summary: Answer the last element; an empty `runes` raises unless a default is given.

members.name: len
members.summary: Answer the number of elements — symbols, not octets.

doc.code: u"abc".len()        // => 3

members.name: lower
members.summary: Map every symbol to lowercase.

doc.code:
u"héllo".upper()                // => u"HÉLLO"
u"HÉLLO".lower()                // => u"héllo"

members.name: map
members.summary: Answer `runes` of the callback's results, strictly 1:1: each result must be exactly one symbol.

doc.markdown:
The callback gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument ([callbacks](kavun:type/runes#callbacks)).

`map` is strictly 1:1 and answers `runes`: the callback must produce exactly **one element** (a rune, an int
that is a valid code point, or a byte — its octet's symbol: ASCII as itself, above it its escape); a sequence or
`undefined` result raises.

doc.code:
u"abc".map(func(r) { return r + 1 })                     // => u"bcd"
u"abc".map(func(i, r) { return i == 0 ? r : r + 1 })     // => u"acd"
u"abc".map(func(r) { return "xy" })                      // Error: invalid_value — map is 1:1; use flat_map
u"abc".map(func(r) { return undefined })                 // Error: invalid_value — the dropping form is flat_map

members.name: max
members.summary: Answer the largest element; an empty `runes` raises unless a default is given.

members.name: min
members.summary: Answer the smallest element; an empty `runes` raises unless a default is given.

members.name: pad_end
members.summary: Pad at the back with the fill element until length `n`; see [`pad_start`](kavun:type/runes/pad_start).

members.name: pad_end_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `pad_end`.

members.name: pad_start
members.summary: Pad at the front with the fill element until length `n`.

doc.markdown:
Width in **symbols**; the fill is exactly **one element** (a run fill would hide a truncation rule — build the
run and append it instead). Default fill is the space. A width at or below the length is a no-op; one past
`4294967296` symbols raises rather than exhausting the host.

doc.code:
u"42".pad_start(5)              // => u"   42"
u"42".pad_start(5, '0')         // => u"00042"
u"ab".pad_end(4, '.')           // => u"ab.."
u"abcdef".pad_start(3)          // => u"abcdef" — no-op
u"ab".pad_start(5, "ab")        // Error: invalid_argument_type — fill is one element

members.name: pad_start_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `pad_start`.

members.name: parse_date
members.summary: Parse the text as a `date` under a layout; text the layout does not read raises unless a default is given.

doc.markdown:
`"date"` reads the strict `YYYY-MM-DD` form, any other layout is read as for [`parse_time`](kavun:type/runes/parse_time) (see
[date](kavun:type/date)); the default comes after the layout.

members.name: parse_time
members.summary: Parse the text as a `time` under a [layout](kavun:type/time#text-layouts); text the layout does not read raises unless a default is given.

doc.markdown: A malformed layout always raises (`invalid_value`). The default comes after the layout.

doc.code: u"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z".parse_time("iso")   // => time("2024-01-02T03:04:05Z") — the canonical grammar

members.name: partition
members.summary: Split at the first separator hit into exactly three pieces, `[before, sep, after]`.

doc.markdown:
`partition` splits at the **first** hit into `[before, separator, after]`; a miss answers `[r, u"", u""]`. With
no argument the separator is the whole first maximal run of blank filler. Separators take the same menu as
[`split`](kavun:type/runes/split); the pieces are `runes`.

doc.code: u"key=value=x".partition("=")   // => [u"key", u"=", u"value=x"]

members.name: pascal_case
members.summary: Render the text as a `PascalCase` identifier; see [`snake_case`](kavun:type/runes/snake_case).

members.name: prepend
members.summary: Add the arguments at the front as whole operands, in argument order; see [`append`](kavun:type/runes/append).

members.name: prepend_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `prepend`.

members.name: push
members.summary: Add each argument at the back as exactly **one element**; a sequence argument raises, even at length 1.

doc.markdown:
`push`/`push_first` are the validating forms: **one element per argument**; a sequence argument raises even at
length 1 — the refusal is the member's purpose (no silent flattening).

doc.code:
u"ab".push('c')                         // => u"abc"
u"ab".push("c")                         // Error: invalid_argument_type — a sequence never reads as one element here
u"ab".push(98)                          // => u"abb" — an int is a code point on the member side
u"ab".push(55296)                       // Error: invalid_value — a surrogate is not a valid code point
u"ab".push(b'\xff')                     // => u"ab\udcff" — a high octet is its escape

members.name: push_first
members.summary: Add each argument at the front as exactly one element, in argument order; see [`push`](kavun:type/runes/push).

members.name: push_first_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `push_first`.

members.name: push_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `push`.

members.name: reduce
members.summary: Fold the elements left to right into an accumulator that starts at `init`.

doc.markdown:
`reduce(init, fn)` folds with the accumulator first. The callback gets `(acc, element)`, or `(acc, index,
element)` when it does not accept two arguments ([callbacks](kavun:type/runes#callbacks)).

doc.code:
u"abc".reduce(0, func(acc, r) { return acc + r.int() })  // => 294
u"ab".reduce(u"".copy(), func(acc, r) { return acc.append(r, r) })  // => u"aabb"

members.name: remove
members.summary: Remove every match of an element, a run, a set or a predicate; with no argument, the elements of the [blank set](kavun:type/runes#the-blank-set).

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/runes#callbacks)).

Both take the full menu and act on **every** occurrence, in the direction their names give: `keep(x)` answers
what matches, `remove(x)` answers what does not. With no argument each reads against the blank set as its own
verb implies: `keep()` keeps the significant symbols, `remove()` removes the blank ones — the same answer by
two different actions. A miss is a silent no-op.

doc.code:
u"banana".keep('a')                           // => u"aaa"
u"banana".remove("an")                          // => u"ba"
u"banana".remove('a', 'b')                      // => u"nn"
u"abcdef".keep(func(i, r) { return i % 2 == 0 })   // => u"ace" — two-parameter form: (index, element)

members.name: remove_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `remove`.

members.name: remove_prefix
members.summary: Remove the element or run — or the longest of a set of them — once, anchored at the front; absent → unchanged.

doc.markdown:
The removals take an element or run — of a set, the longest that matches — remove it **once**, and answer the
receiver unchanged on a miss.

doc.code:
u"foobar".remove_prefix("foo")          // => u"bar"
u"foobar".remove_prefix("bar")          // => u"foobar" — miss → unchanged
u"foobar".remove_suffix("bar")          // => u"foo"
u"abcd".remove_prefix("ab", "abc")      // => u"d" — longest run wins the tie

members.name: remove_prefix_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `remove_prefix`.

members.name: remove_suffix
members.summary: Remove the element or run — or the longest of a set of them — once, anchored at the back; absent → unchanged; see [`remove_prefix`](kavun:type/runes/remove_prefix).

members.name: remove_suffix_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `remove_suffix`.

members.name: repeat
members.summary: Concatenate the receiver with itself `n` times; `u * n` is the operator form.

doc.markdown:
`repeat(n)` takes a whole-number count (`2.0` converts, `1.5` raises) and has the operator form `u * n` (no
reflected `n * u`).

doc.code:
u"ab".repeat(2)                 // => u"abab"
u"ab".repeat(1.5)               // Error: invalid_value — never silent truncation

members.name: replace
members.summary: Replace every occurrence of `old`, an element or a run, with `new`.

doc.markdown:
Element or run in both positions; every occurrence, leftmost, non-overlapping. Never variadic (the second
position is the replacement), never a predicate.

doc.code:
u"a-b-c".replace("-", " / ")    // => u"a / b / c"
u"a-b-c".replace('-', '+')      // => u"a+b+c"

members.name: replace_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `replace`.

members.name: reverse
members.summary: Reverse the order of the elements.

doc.code: u"abc".reverse()                // => u"cba"

members.name: reverse_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `reverse`.

members.name: runes
members.summary: Answer a new, independent, mutable copy, exactly `runes(r)` / `r.copy()`.

doc.code: u"ab".runes()           // a NEW, independent, mutable copy — same as runes(r), not the receiver

doc.markdown:
The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

members.name: slice
members.summary: Answer a copy of the elements from `start` to `end`; bounds **clamp** (contrast `splice`, which raises), negative indices count from the end.

doc.markdown: `slice(i, j)` **clamps** — reading past the end is harmless.

doc.code:
u"abcdef".slice(1, 3)           // => u"bc"
u"abc".slice(1, 99)             // => u"bc" — clamps
u"abcdef".slice(-3, -1)         // => u"de"

members.name: slice_view
members.summary: Answer the elements from `start` to `end` as a view sharing the receiver's storage, so mutation flows both ways.

doc.markdown: The sharing twin of [`slice`](kavun:type/runes/slice): a write through the view is visible in the original.

doc.code:
sv := u"abcdef".copy()
v := sv.slice_view(1, 3)        // shares storage
v[0] = 'X'                      // sv is now u"aXcdef"

members.name: snake_case
members.summary: Render the text as a `snake_case` identifier.

doc.markdown:
The identifier renderings (`snake_case`, `kebab_case`, `camel_case`, `pascal_case`) segment **fully**: on written
boundaries (runs of whitespace / `_` / `-`, discarded), on lower→upper transitions, and before the last upper of
an upper-run followed by lowers (`parseXMLFile` → `parse|XML|File`). The boundary set is closed — digits,
apostrophes, and periods stay inside their word. Word interiors are normalised to the rendering's case.

doc.code:
u"parseXMLFile".snake_case()        // => u"parse_xml_file"
u"parseXMLFile".kebab_case()        // => u"parse-xml-file"
u"parse XML file".camel_case()      // => u"parseXmlFile"
u"parse XML file".pascal_case()     // => u"ParseXmlFile"
u"Hello  World-Wide".snake_case()   // => u"hello_world_wide"
u"utf8 codec v2".snake_case()       // => u"utf8_codec_v2" — digits stay inside

members.name: sort
members.summary: Sort the symbols by code point; there is no comparator.

doc.code: u"cba".sort()                   // => u"abc"

members.name: sort_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `sort`.

members.name: splice
members.summary: Removes `delete_count` elements at `start`, then inserts the items there.

doc.markdown:
`splice(start[, count, ...items])` is the positional edit: a `start` outside `[0, len]` **raises**, a negative
`count` raises, the `count` clamps to what is available; omitted `count` means "to the end". Splice's inserts take
the add-side reading — a text-run argument spreads, one element stays one element.

doc.code:
u"abcd".splice(1, 2, "XY")      // => u"aXYd"
u"ad".splice(1, 0, "bc", 'x')   // => u"abcxd" — runs spread, elements insert
u"ab".splice(3, 0)              // Error: index_out_of_bounds: (splice, start index) 3 out of range [0, 2]
u"abcd".splice(1)               // => u"a" — no count: delete to the end

members.name: splice_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `splice`.

members.name: split
members.summary: Split the text into an array of the pieces between the separators.

doc.markdown:
Separators come from the dispatch menu: element, run, homogeneous variadic set, element-level predicate, or
absent (= the blank set). **Explicit separators keep empty pieces** — n hits produce n+1 pieces; the no-arg
blank form separates on runs of whitespace and drops empties. An empty-run separator matches nothing. There
is **no limit argument**. The pieces are `runes`.

doc.code:
u"a,,b".split(',')              // => [u"a", u"", u"b"] — empties kept
u"a::b::c".split("::")          // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"]
u"a,b;c".split(',', ';')        // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"] — element set
u"a,b;c".split(',', "::")       // Error: invalid_argument_type — mixed element + run set
u"a1b2c".split(func(r) { return r >= '0' && r <= '9' })  // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"]
u"  a b \t c ".split()          // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"] — blank separators, empties dropped
u"ab".split("")                 // => [u"ab"] — an empty run matches nothing

members.name: split_lines
members.summary: Split the text into an array of its lines at `\n`, `\r\n` or `\r`; a trailing line break adds no empty last line.

doc.code:
u"a
b
c".split_lines()      // => [u"a", u"b", u"c"]
u"a

b".split_lines()         // => [u"a", u"", u"b"] — interior empty lines kept

members.name: string
members.summary: Re-encode the symbols as a `string`; total.

doc.code: u"héllo".string()       // => "héllo" — re-encode — total

doc.markdown:
The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

members.name: time
members.summary: Parse the text as a `time` in the canonical grammar, as `time(text)` reads it; bad text raises unless a default is given.

doc.markdown: Any other spelling names its layout: see [`parse_time`](kavun:type/runes/parse_time).

members.name: title_case
members.summary: Render the text as a label: each word's first symbol uppercased, the interior preserved.

doc.markdown:
`title_case` is the label rendering: it segments on the **written** boundaries only (each separator run becomes a
single space), uppercases each word's first symbol, and **preserves the interior** — a label keeps the author's
emphasis; case transitions never split a word.

doc.code:
u"ATM fee".title_case()         // => u"ATM Fee"
u"iPhone".title_case()          // => u"IPhone"
u"hELLO world".title_case()     // => u"HELLO World"
u"per_diem rate".title_case()   // => u"Per Diem Rate"

members.name: trim
members.summary: Repeatedly drop the elements at both ends while they belong to the set (the blank set with no argument).

doc.markdown:
The trim family takes a **set of elements** and strips while members of the set repeat at the edge. A run
argument raises — the anchored run form is `remove_prefix`/`remove_suffix`. No arguments = the blank set.

doc.code:
u"xxhixx".trim('x')             // => u"hi"
u"xyhixy".trim('x', 'y')        // => u"hi"
u"xyhixy".trim("xy")            // Error: invalid_argument_type: trim takes a set of elements, not a run
u"  hi  ".trim_start()          // => u"hi  "
u"  hi  ".trim_end()            // => u"  hi"

members.name: trim_end
members.summary: Drop the trailing elements that belong to the set (the blank set with no argument); see [`trim`](kavun:type/runes/trim).

members.name: trim_end_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `trim_end`.

members.name: trim_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `trim`.

members.name: trim_start
members.summary: Drop the leading elements that belong to the set (the blank set with no argument); see [`trim`](kavun:type/runes/trim).

members.name: trim_start_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `trim_start`.

members.name: unique
members.summary: Drop repeats, keeping each element at its first occurrence.

doc.code: u"aabbaa".unique()              // => u"ab"

members.name: unique_in_place
members.summary: In-place twin of `unique`.

members.name: upper
members.summary: Map every symbol to uppercase; see [`lower`](kavun:type/runes/lower).

types.name: string
types.summary: Immutable Unicode text.

doc.markdown:
## Overview

A `string` is a sequence of **symbols** (Unicode code points). The symbol is the element everywhere on the
type: `len()` counts symbols, `s[i]` yields a `rune`, `s[i:j]` slices at symbol boundaries, and every member
offset — `index()`, `slice()`, `splice()`, `insert()` — is symbol-based.

doc.code:
"héllo".len()        // => 5 — symbols, not bytes
"héllo"[1]           // => 'é' — a rune
"héllo"[1:3]         // => "él"
"abc"[-1]            // => 'c' — negative indices count from the end
"кавун".len()        // => 5

doc.markdown:
Symbols are code points, **not** grapheme clusters. A flag emoji is two regional-indicator symbols; a
combining sequence is a base symbol plus combining marks. What a reader perceives as one character can be
several symbols:

doc.code:
"🇺🇦".len()          // => 2 — two regional indicators
"e\u0301".len()     // => 2 — é written as e + U+0301 (combining acute)

doc.markdown:
**Storage and cost.** A `string` is stored as compact UTF-8 with a cached symbol count and an ASCII fast
path: indexing and slicing are O(1) on pure-ASCII strings and O(n) worst case on multibyte content. For heavy
positional work on non-ASCII text, convert to [`runes`](kavun:type/runes) first — `runes` is the O(1)-indexing,
materialized form of the same text.
Members whose answer depends on the ends of the text or on the argument alone — `first`/`last`, the anchored pair
and their `remove_` twins, the `trim` family, the pads, and `contains`/`count`/`index`/`index_last`/`replace` —
read the text in place and never decode the whole receiver; the members that visit or rebuild every symbol decode
it once per call.

**Immutability.** A `string` is immutable by construction. It is the only sequence type with no mutating
member at all: no `_in_place` twins, and no `slice_view`/`chunk_view` (on an immutable value sharing is
unobservable, so `slice` *is* the view). Element assignment raises:

doc.code:
s := "abc"
s[0] = 'x'           // Error: not_assignable: type string does not support assignment

doc.markdown:
A `string` literal is a compile-time constant as well: its content is fixed in the source, so the compiler
stores it once in the bytecode's static pool and every evaluation loads that one shared value. For `string`
this is invisible — the type has no mutating member either way — but it is the same mechanism that makes
`b"..."` and `u"..."` immutable *constants* of otherwise mutable types, and the reason all three short forms
exist: text written down in a program is usually constant text. See [Constant literals and constructed
literals](kavun:doc/language#constant-literals-and-constructed-literals); when you want a mutable buffer of the
same content, construct one — `runes("abc")` or `bytes("abc")`.

**`string` and `runes` are semantically interchangeable** — the same text, the same member surface, the same
operator behavior, and they compare equal on equal content (`"ab" == u"ab"` is `true`). The difference is
storage (UTF-8 vs. a symbol array) and mutability. Choose `string` by default; choose `runes` when you need
in-place mutation or guaranteed O(1) indexing.

Every transforming member returns a new `string`; partitioning members (`split`, `partition`, `split_lines`,
`chunk`) return an `array` of strings.

The edge members `first([d])`, `last([d])`, `min([d])` and `max([d])` answer a `rune`; an empty string has no edge
to give, so without the optional trailing default they raise `invalid_value`:

doc.code:
"abc".first()        // => 'a'
"".first()           // Error: invalid_value: (first) empty sequence
"".first('?')        // => '?'
"banana".min()       // => 'a'
"banana".max()       // => 'n'

doc.markdown:
The parsing conversions (`int`, `float`, `decimal`, `bool`, `time`, `date`, `nanoseconds`) follow the uniform
failure policy: a valid result or a catchable raise, and with the optional trailing default, the default when the
text does not parse. A malformed `time`/`date` layout is the caller's error, not the data's, and raises even with a
default. The re-representations `runes()`, `bytes()` and `array()` are total — they cannot fail — so they take no
default.

## Literals

doc.code:
s := "hello"
esc := "line1\nline2 \"quoted\" \u00a0"   // escape sequences
raw := r"C:\Users\Bob \d+"                 // raw string: backslashes literal
uni := u"кавун"                             // a runes literal — same text, runes type

doc.markdown:
The free `string(x)` constructor is the conversion — the free spelling of `x.string()`. The two-argument
`string(x, n)` is the count form: the conversion repeated `n` times, `string(x).repeat(n)`:

doc.code:
string()             // => ""
string("ab", 2)      // => "abab" — the count form: string(x).repeat(n)
string('x', 3)       // => "xxx"
string(65, 2)        // => "6565" — the conversion first: string(65) is "65"

doc.markdown:
F-strings interpolate expressions and format specs into a `string`: `f"n={n:5d}"`. See
[f-strings](kavun:doc/f_strings) and the [format mini-language](kavun:doc/format_mini_language).

## Operators

| operator | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `+` | concatenation of text content |
| `-` | remove every occurrence of the run (leftmost, non-overlapping), read as symbols as `remove` reads it — the octets of an escape never match inside a symbol; acceptance equals `+`'s |
| `*` | exactly `repeat(n)`: the right operand is a **count**, not text. No reflected direction — `n * s` raises |
| `==` `!=` | content equality; `string` and `runes` with the same text are equal |
| `<` `<=` `>` `>=` | lexicographic by symbol |
| `x in s` | membership — runs `contains`' value readings |
| `s[i]` | the symbol at `i`, as a `rune` |
| `s[i:j]` | symbol-boundary slice, a `string` |

Both operands must carry **text content**. The **receiver (left operand) decides the result type**; a scalar
on the left takes the sequence's type:

doc.code:
"ab" + "cd"          // => "abcd"
"ab" + u"cd"         // => "abcd" — string — the left operand decides
u"ab" + "cd"         // => u"abcd" — runes on the left
"ab" + bytes("cd")   // => "abcd" — the bytes decode; the decode never fails
b'a' + "bc"          // => "abc" — scalar left takes the sequence's type
'é' + "bc"           // => "ébc"
"abc" + b'\xff'      // => "abc\xff" — the octet, as + bytes([255]) adds it
"ab" + 1             // Error: invalid_binary_operator: operators never take int — arithmetic keeps its reading
"ab" + 1.5           // Error: invalid_binary_operator
"ab" + true          // Error: invalid_binary_operator
"ab" + ["cd"]        // => ["ab", "cd"] — string declines; the array prepends it as one element
"ab" - ["cd"]        // Error: invalid_binary_operator: string - array (there is no reflected form for removal)

doc.markdown: `-` removes runs or single symbols, never set-difference:

doc.code:
"banana" - "na"      // => "ba" — every occurrence, leftmost non-overlapping
"banana" - 'a'       // => "bnn"
"banana" - 97        // Error: invalid_binary_operator: operators never take int

"-" * 20             // => "--------------------" — the count form of repeat
"ab" * 2.0           // => "abab" — a whole-valued count converts; 1.5 raises
2 * "ab"             // Error: invalid_binary_operator: int * string   (no reflected direction)

doc.markdown:
`in` accepts exactly the values `contains` accepts and raises on anything else — a callable raises, because
an operator operand is always a value, never a predicate:

doc.code:
'a' in "abc"                       // => true
"bc" in "abc"                      // => true
97 in "abc"                        // => true — 'a' — members read a valid int as the symbol
1.5 in "abc"                       // Error: invalid_argument_type
(func(c) { return true }) in "abc" // Error: invalid_value — the predicate spelling is contains(f)

doc.markdown: Comparisons are lexicographic by symbol, not by length:

doc.code:
"abc" < "abd"        // => true
"b" > "aaaa"         // => true

doc.markdown:
## Argument dispatch

Every member and operator on `string` reads its arguments the same way. An argument is accepted iff it is
**text content encoded into the receiver's representation**:

| argument | reading |
| --- | --- |
| `string` / `runes` | text, verbatim — a contiguous **run** |
| `bytes` | decoded as UTF-8; **total** — an octet that is not a symbol becomes its [escape](kavun:type/string#undecodable-octets) |
| `rune` | itself — one symbol |
| `byte` | its octet, as `bytes([b])` — one symbol in ASCII, its [escape](kavun:type/string#undecodable-octets) above |
| `int` (members only) | one symbol iff a valid code point; **operators never take `int`** |
| `bool` / `float` / `decimal` | raise — a number as text is ambiguous (`65` could be `"65"` or `'A'`) |
| `int` (`*` only) | a repeat **count** — `s * n` is exactly `s.repeat(n)`; there is no reflected `n * s` |
| `array` / `range` / `dict` / callables / `undefined` | raise — the text family is closed. One exception is not `string`'s doing: `"ab" + [1, 2]` → `["ab", 1, 2]`, because a left operand that declines hands `+` to the array, which prepends it as one element (see [array](kavun:type/array)) |

The match members (`contains`, `count`, `index`, `index_last`, `keep`, `remove`, `any`, `all`, `split`, …)
share one argument menu:

- **no argument** — the [blank set](kavun:type/string#the-blank-set);
- **a function** — a predicate: it gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks));
- **`string`/`runes`/`bytes`** — a contiguous run;
- **`rune`/`byte`/valid `int`** — one element (a byte is its octet: ASCII as its symbol, above it its
[escape](kavun:type/string#undecodable-octets));
- **variadic** — a homogeneous set: all elements or all runs. Mixing the two classes raises, and a function
among several arguments raises.

doc.code:
"abc".contains('x', 'b')                       // => true — element set
"abc".count(func(i, c) { return i > 0 })       // => 2 — accepts two, not one: gets (index, element)
"abcd".remove("ab", "abc")                     // => "d" — run set; at a tie the longest run wins
"banana".remove("na", 'b')                     // Error: invalid_argument_type: mixed element and run classes
"abc".remove("a", func(c) { return true })     // Error: invalid_argument_type: a function among several arguments

doc.markdown:
The one exception is the **add side** (`append`/`prepend`), where operands mix freely in order:
`x.append("ab", 'c')` ≡ `x + "ab" + 'c'`.

Run matching is leftmost and non-overlapping: `"aaa".count("aa")` is `1`.

## Undecodable octets

Text that is not valid UTF-8 is data too — a file off disk, a legacy export, a truncated frame. So **every
conversion among `byte`, `bytes`, `string` and `runes` is total and lossless**: nothing raises, nothing is
substituted, and the octets you started with are the octets you get back.

An octet no decoder can read as a symbol becomes its own reserved rune — **U+DC80–U+DCFF, one per octet
0x80–0xFF** — and encoding turns that rune straight back into the octet it came from.

doc.code:
b = bytes([0x61, 0xFF, 0x62])   // 'a', a stray octet, 'b'
s = b.string()                  // no raise
s.len()                         // => 3 — the octet is one symbol
s[1].int()                      // => 56575 — U+DCFF, the escape for 0xFF
s.bytes() == b                  // => true
s.runes().bytes() == b          // => true — through runes and back, unchanged

doc.markdown: Asking, and repairing:

doc.code:
s := bytes([0x61, 0xFF, 0x62]).string()
s.is_valid()                    // => false — some symbol is an escape
"abc".is_valid()                // => true
s[1].is_valid()                 // => false — this one
s[1].byte()                     // => byte(255) — the escape converts back to its octet
s.replace(s[1], '?')            // => "a?b"
s.keep(c => c.is_valid())     // => "ab"

doc.markdown:
**Spelling one in source.** A `string` literal holds octets, so it writes the octet: `"\xff"`. A rune literal
and a runes literal hold symbols, so they write the escape rune: `'\udcff'`, `u"\udcff"` (or `\U0000DCFF`).
`"\udcff"` is a parse error that names `\xff` as the spelling to use; every other surrogate (`\ud800`,
`\udc7f`, ...) is a parse error in every literal, and `bytes`/`byte` literals take only `\xNN`. The `v` render of
each type writes these same spellings, so it always reads back as the value it came from.

doc.code:
"\xff"[0] == '\udcff'          // => true
"\xff".runes() == u"\udcff"     // => true
"\xff".runes().format("v")      // => "u\"\\udcff\""

doc.markdown:
**Why this range, and why it cannot go wrong.** Only an octet ≥ 0x80 can ever be undecodable — an ASCII octet
is always a symbol — so 128 values suffice. Every undecodable octet decodes with width 1, so *n* bad octets
always become *n* escapes. And U+DC80–U+DCFF are low surrogates: never Unicode scalar values, so well-formed
text can never produce one and an escape can never be mistaken for content. (The scheme is Python's
`surrogateescape`, PEP 383; Rust's WTF-8 answers the same problem the same way.)

**A string is its octets, so building one joins octets.** Every member and operator that builds a string — `+`,
`append`, `prepend`, `push`, `replace`, `pad_start`/`pad_end`, f-strings — concatenates the octets, and the result is
read afresh: escapes whose octets meet to complete a sequence read as the one symbol they spell.
[`runes`](kavun:type/runes) holds symbols, so the same building keeps them apart; the octets are the same either
way.

doc.code:
a = bytes([0xE2, 0x82]).string()  // two escapes: the first two octets of "₩"
b = bytes([0xA9]).string()        // one escape: its last octet
(a + b).len()                     // => 1 — the octets meet and read "₩"
a + b == "₩"                      // => true
a.runes().append(b).len()         // => 3 — runes keeps the three escapes

doc.markdown:
**The two places this is visible elsewhere.** A [`rune`](kavun:type/rune)'s domain is exactly what can be encoded
— scalar values plus the 128 escapes — so `rune(0xDCFF)` exists while `rune(0xD800)` raises where it is written, and
no conversion *out* of `rune`/`runes` can fail. And the boundary **out** of the language is not total: `json.encode`
raises on text holding escapes, because JSON text is UTF-8 by definition. Encode the `bytes` instead (they go as
base64), or repair the text first.

## The blank set

The no-argument form of the match members acts on the type's **blank set** — its notion of insignificant
content. For `string` that is **NUL ∪ Unicode whitespace** (the Unicode `White_Space` class): this is what
no-arg `trim()`, `split()`, `partition()`, `index()`, `count()`, `keep()`, and `remove()` act on, and the
default `pad_start`/`pad_end` fill is the set's canonical member, the space.

Being the Unicode class, it includes the non-breaking space and every other Unicode space — not just ASCII
whitespace:

doc.code:
"\u00a0x".trim()     // => "x" — the NBSP is blank
"\x00x\x00".trim()   // => "x" — NUL is blank

doc.markdown:
`bytes` projects the same notion into its element domain (the ASCII subset — all the whitespace an octet can
express); the sets agree wherever the domains overlap.

## Callbacks

A member that takes a function — the predicate reading of the match members, `map`, `flat_map`, `for_each`, `reduce`
— calls it in the **fewest form it accepts**, read from the callable's arity and whether it is variadic, never from
what kind of callable it is:

- a per-element callback gets the element when it accepts one argument, else `(index, element)`; anything else
raises;
- a `reduce` callback gets `(acc, element)` when it accepts two arguments, else `(acc, index, element)`; anything
else raises.

So `func(x, ...rest)` and `func(...args)` get the element, and a builtin or a bound member is a callback like any
other (`min` and `"abc".contains` accept one argument). A lambda is the one way to call a callable in another form —
choose the form, reorder, fix or drop arguments:

doc.code:
"abc".count(func(i, c) { return i > 0 })               // => 2 — accepts two, not one
"abc".index(func(c, ...rest) { return c == 'b' })     // => 1 — accepts one: the element
"abcd".keep("bd".contains)                            // => "bd"
"abc".reduce("", (s, c) => c + s)                      // => "cba"

members.name: all
members.summary: Report whether every element matches a value, a set or a predicate; with no argument, whether every element is significant; see [`any`](kavun:type/string/any).

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

members.name: any
members.summary: Report whether some element matches a value, a set or a predicate; with no argument, whether any element is significant.

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

`any`/`all` take a value, a function, or nothing — the contiguous-run query belongs to `contains`:

doc.code:
"abc".all(func(c) { return c >= 'a' })    // => true
"abc".any("ab")              // Error: invalid_argument_type: "all/any of a run" has no reading — use contains

members.name: append
members.summary: Add the arguments at the back as whole operands: text spreads as a run, a symbol is one element.

doc.markdown:
`x.append(a, b)` ≡ `x + a + b`.

Whole operands in order, mixing runs and elements freely: `x.append("ab", 'c')` ≡ `x + "ab" + 'c'`.

doc.code:
"x".append("ab", 'c', 98)    // => "xabcb" — 98 is 'b'
"ab".append(bytes("cd"))     // => "abcd"
"c".prepend("a", 'b')        // => "abc" — arguments in order, at the front

members.name: array
members.summary: Re-represent the text as an array of its symbols, each a `rune`.

doc.code: "abé".array()        // => ['a', 'b', 'é'] — an array of runes

doc.markdown:
The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

members.name: bool
members.summary: Parse the text as a `bool`: `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`, `t`/`f`, `yes`/`no`, case-insensitive.

doc.code:
"Yes".bool()         // => true — true/false, 1/0, t/f, yes/no — case-insensitive
"maybe".bool()       // Error: conversion

members.name: bytes
members.summary: Re-represent the text as its octets, the UTF-8 encoding.

doc.code: "héllo".bytes().len()  // => 6 — octets — the UTF-8 encoding

doc.markdown:
The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

members.name: camel_case
members.summary: Render the text as a `camelCase` identifier; see [`snake_case`](kavun:type/string/snake_case).

members.name: case_fold
members.summary: Answer the canonical case fold, so that `a.case_fold() == b.case_fold()` is exact case-insensitive equality.

doc.markdown:
`case_fold()` is the canonical fold: each fold orbit maps to its smallest lowercase member (else the smallest
member), so `a.case_fold() == b.case_fold()` is exact case-insensitive equality. Because it is a transform —
not a comparison predicate — the result composes: it works as a dict key, a sort basis, a dedup basis.
`.lower()` comparison is not a substitute; they differ in both directions:

doc.code:
"Hello".case_fold()                                   // => "hello"
"ſtraße".case_fold() == "Straße".case_fold()          // => true — long s ſ and S both fold to s
"İstanbul".case_fold() == "istanbul".case_fold()      // => false — İ keeps its own identity, distinct from i

members.name: chunk
members.summary: Split into strings of up to `n` symbols, answered as an array.

doc.code: "abcde".chunk(2)             // => ["ab", "cd", "e"]

members.name: contains
members.summary: Report whether an element, a run, a member of a set or a predicate match occurs; with no argument, whether any element is significant.

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

It takes all five readings: element, run, variadic set, predicate, and no-argument (any element outside the blank
set).

No-argument `contains()` ≡ `any()` asks "any significant content?" — `"   ".contains()` is `false`. The
contiguous-run query belongs to `contains`: `any`/`all` take no run.

doc.code: "banana".contains("nan")     // => true

members.name: copy
members.summary: Answer the receiver, which as an immutable string already is an independent copy.

doc.markdown: On an immutable value `copy`/`freeze` are cheap identity-like operations kept for generic code.

members.name: count
members.summary: Count the matches of an element, a run (non-overlapping occurrences), a set or a predicate; with no argument, the significant elements.

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

doc.code: "banana".count("na")         // => 2

members.name: date
members.summary: Parse the text as a `date` in the strict `YYYY-MM-DD` form, as `date(text)` reads it; bad text raises unless a default is given.

doc.markdown: Any other spelling names its layout: see [`parse_date`](kavun:type/string/parse_date).

members.name: decimal
members.summary: Parse the text as a `decimal`; bad text raises unless a default is given.

members.name: dedup
members.summary: Collapse each run of equal neighbours to one element.

doc.code: "aabbaa".dedup()             // => "aba"

members.name: first
members.summary: Answer the first element; an empty string raises unless a default is given.

members.name: flat_map
members.summary: Map each element through the callback, then concatenate: a run result splices in, `undefined` is dropped.

doc.markdown: The callback gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument ([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

doc.code:
"a-b".flat_map(func(c) { return c == '-' ? " / " : c })  // => "a / b"
"a-b".flat_map(func(c) { return c == '-' ? undefined : c })  // => "ab" — undefined dropped

members.name: float
members.summary: Parse the text as a `float`; bad text raises unless a default is given.

members.name: for_each
members.summary: Call the callback on every element — always a **full pass**, its return value ignored — and return the receiver.

doc.markdown:
The callback gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument ([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

Early exit is `break`'s job in a `for` loop; returning the receiver lets it chain.

doc.code:
io := import("io")
"abc".for_each(func(c) { io.print(c) })               // prints each symbol, returns "abc"

members.name: format
members.summary: Render the value per the [format mini-language](kavun:doc/format_mini_language).

doc.code: "hi".format("q")     // => "\"hi\"" — quoted render

members.name: freeze
members.summary: Answer the receiver, which as a string already is deep-immutable; see [`copy`](kavun:type/string/copy).

doc.code: is_immutable("abc")  // => true — free predicate — always, for string

members.name: has_prefix
members.summary: Report whether the string starts with the element or run, or with any of a set of them.

doc.markdown: No predicate reading ("the first symbol satisfies `f`" is `index(f) == 0`).

doc.code:
"foobar".has_prefix('f')            // => true
"foobar".has_prefix("x", "fo")      // => true — run set

members.name: has_suffix
members.summary: Report whether the string ends with the element or run, or with any of a set of them; see [`has_prefix`](kavun:type/string/has_prefix).

members.name: index
members.summary: Answer the first position of a match of an element, a run or a predicate, or `undefined` (the `default` when given) on a miss.

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

`index` and [`index_last`](kavun:type/string/index_last) are the only locators.

A locator miss answers `undefined` — never `-1` — or the trailing default. The position is a symbol offset,
usable with `s[i]`.

doc.code:
"banana".index("na")         // => 2
"banana".index_last("na")    // => 4
"banana".index("xy")         // => undefined — miss — never -1
"banana".index("xy", -1)     // => -1 — explicit default
"héllo".index('l')           // => 2 — symbol offset, usable with s[i]
"abc".index(func(c) { return c == 'b' })  // => 1
"  ab".index()               // => 2 — no argument: first significant symbol

members.name: index_last
members.summary: Answer the last position of a match, or `undefined` (the `default` when given) on a miss; see [`index`](kavun:type/string/index).

members.name: insert
members.summary: Insert each argument as one element at position `i`.

doc.markdown: An edit position out of `[0, len]` raises.

doc.code:
"ad".insert(1, 'b', 'c')     // => "abcd"
"ab".insert(2, 'c')          // => "abc" — position len is valid
"ab".insert(3, 'c')          // Error: index_out_of_bounds: 3 out of range [0, 2]

members.name: int
members.summary: Parse the text as an `int`; bad text raises unless a default is given.

doc.code:
"123".int()          // => 123
"12a".int()          // Error: conversion: cannot convert string to int
"12a".int(0)         // => 0

members.name: is_ascii
members.summary: Report whether every octet is below `0x80`, which also means one octet per symbol.

doc.code:
"abc".is_ascii()                      // => true
"abé".is_ascii()                      // => false

members.name: is_empty
members.summary: Report whether the string has no elements.

members.name: is_true
members.summary: Report truthiness, which is non-emptiness: `!!x` ⟺ `x != string()`.

members.name: is_valid
members.summary: Report whether every symbol is a real symbol, with no [octet escapes](kavun:type/string#undecodable-octets).

doc.markdown: The text is well-formed UTF-8 exactly when this holds.

doc.code:
"abc".is_valid()                      // => true
bytes([97, 255]).string().is_valid()  // => false

members.name: kebab_case
members.summary: Render the text as a `kebab-case` identifier; see [`snake_case`](kavun:type/string/snake_case).

members.name: keep
members.summary: Keep only the matches of an element, a run, a set or a predicate; with no argument, the significant elements; see [`remove`](kavun:type/string/remove).

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

members.name: last
members.summary: Answer the last element; an empty string raises unless a default is given.

members.name: len
members.summary: Answer the number of elements — symbols, not octets.

members.name: lower
members.summary: Map every symbol to lowercase.

doc.code:
"héllo".upper()      // => "HÉLLO"
"HÉLLO".lower()      // => "héllo"

members.name: map
members.summary: Answer a `string` of the callback's results, strictly 1:1: each result must be exactly one symbol.

doc.markdown:
The callback gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument ([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

The callback must return exactly one symbol per element — a rune, an int that is a valid code point, or a byte
(its octet: ASCII as its symbol, above it the octet itself); a sequence or `undefined` result raises.

doc.code:
"abc".map(func(c) { return (c.int() + 1).rune() })       // => "bcd"
"abc".map(func(c) { return "xx" })   // Error: invalid_value: map is 1:1 — the concatenating form is flat_map

members.name: max
members.summary: Answer the largest element; an empty string raises unless a default is given.

members.name: min
members.summary: Answer the smallest element; an empty string raises unless a default is given.

members.name: nanoseconds
members.summary: Parse the text as a duration in nanoseconds, in Go's duration grammar (`"300ms"`, `"-1.5h"`).

doc.code:
"1h30m".nanoseconds()    // => 5400000000000 — a duration, in Go's duration grammar ("300ms", "-1.5h")
"later".nanoseconds(0)   // => 0

members.name: pad_end
members.summary: Pad at the back with the fill element until length `n`; see [`pad_start`](kavun:type/string/pad_start).

members.name: pad_start
members.summary: Pad at the front with the fill element until length `n`.

doc.markdown:
Pad to symbol width `n` with one fill element (default: the space, the blank set's canonical member). A run fill
raises; a width at or below `len()` is a no-op, and one past `4294967296` symbols raises rather than exhausting
the host.

doc.code:
"7".pad_start(3)                    // => "  7"
"7".pad_start(3, '0')               // => "007"
"7".pad_start(3, "ab")              // Error: invalid_argument_type: one fill element, not a run

members.name: parse_date
members.summary: Parse the text as a `date` under a layout; text the layout does not read raises unless a default is given.

doc.markdown:
`"date"` reads the strict `YYYY-MM-DD` form, any other layout is read as for [`parse_time`](kavun:type/string/parse_time) (see
[date](kavun:type/date)); the default comes after the layout.

members.name: parse_time
members.summary: Parse the text as a `time` under a [layout](kavun:type/time#text-layouts); text the layout does not read raises unless a default is given.

doc.markdown:
A malformed layout always raises (`invalid_value`): it is the script's mistake, not the data's. The default
comes after the layout.

doc.code:
"2026-08-29T00:00:00Z".parse_time("iso").year()   // => 2026 — the canonical grammar
"29/08/2026".parse_time("%d/%m/%Y").day()          // => 29
"nope".parse_time("iso", time())                   // => time("1970-01-01T00:00:00Z") — the default, after the layout

members.name: partition
members.summary: Split at the first separator hit into exactly three pieces, `[before, sep, after]`.

doc.markdown:
`partition` answers exactly three pieces, `[before, sep, after]`, splitting at the first hit; a miss answers
`[s, "", ""]`. With no argument the separator is the whole first maximal run of blank filler. Separators take
the same menu as [`split`](kavun:type/string/split).

doc.code:
"key=value=x".partition('=')     // => ["key", "=", "value=x"]
"abc".partition('=')             // => ["abc", "", ""]
"key  value rest".partition()    // => ["key", "  ", "value rest"]

members.name: pascal_case
members.summary: Render the text as a `PascalCase` identifier; see [`snake_case`](kavun:type/string/snake_case).

members.name: prepend
members.summary: Add the arguments at the front as whole operands, in argument order; see [`append`](kavun:type/string/append).

members.name: push
members.summary: Add each argument at the back as exactly **one element**; a sequence argument raises, even at length 1.

doc.markdown: **Validating**: the refusal is the member's purpose — use it when appending a run would be a bug.

doc.code:
"ab".push('c')               // => "abc"
"ab".push("c")               // Error: invalid_argument_type: push takes one element, never a sequence

members.name: push_first
members.summary: Add each argument at the front as exactly one element, in argument order; see [`push`](kavun:type/string/push).

members.name: reduce
members.summary: Fold the elements left to right into an accumulator that starts at `init`.

doc.markdown:
The callback gets `(acc, element)`, or `(acc, index, element)` when it does not accept two arguments
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

doc.code: "abc".reduce(0, func(acc, c) { return acc + c.int() })   // => 294

members.name: remove
members.summary: Remove every match of an element, a run, a set or a predicate; with no argument, the elements of the [blank set](kavun:type/string#the-blank-set).

doc.markdown:
A function argument gets the element, or `(index, element)` when it does not accept one argument
([callbacks](kavun:type/string#callbacks)).

`remove` and [`keep`](kavun:type/string/keep) are duals over the same readings, and the names say which way each one goes.

`keep(x)` answers the matching symbols, `remove(x)` answers the rest — the direction is in the name; both take
the full menu and act on every occurrence. With no argument each reads against the blank set the way its own
verb implies — `keep()` keeps the significant symbols, `remove()` removes the blank ones — so the two land on
the same answer by two different routes:

doc.code:
"a1b2".keep(func(c) { return c >= '0' && c <= '9' })   // => "12"
"banana".remove("na")        // => "ba"
" a b ".keep()             // => "ab"
" a b ".remove()             // => "ab" — removes the blanks — same answer, the other action

members.name: remove_prefix
members.summary: Remove the element or run — or the longest of a set of them — once, anchored at the front; absent → unchanged.

doc.markdown: Given several, the longest that matches is removed; a miss answers the receiver unchanged.

doc.code:
"foobar".remove_prefix("foo")       // => "bar"
"foobar".remove_prefix("bar")       // => "foobar" — miss: unchanged
"file.txt".remove_suffix(".txt", ".md")  // => "file"

members.name: remove_suffix
members.summary: Remove the element or run — or the longest of a set of them — once, anchored at the back; absent → unchanged; see [`remove_prefix`](kavun:type/string/remove_prefix).

members.name: repeat
members.summary: Concatenate the string with itself `n` times; `s * n` is the operator form.

doc.markdown:
`n` must be a non-negative whole number (`2.0` converts, `1.5` raises). `s * n` is the operator form — same
count slot, same errors. There is no reflected `n * s`, and a result past `4294967296` symbols raises rather
than exhausting the host.

doc.code:
"ab".repeat(3)               // => "ababab"
"ab" * 3                     // => "ababab" — the operator form
"-" * 40                     // => "----------------------------------------"
3 * "ab"                     // Error: invalid_binary_operator: int * string — no reflected direction
"ab".repeat(1.5)             // Error: invalid_value: whole number required — never silent truncation

members.name: replace
members.summary: Replace every occurrence of `old`, an element or a run, with `new`.

doc.markdown: Element or run in both positions; never variadic, never a predicate.

doc.code:
"banana".replace("na", "NO")        // => "baNONO"
"banana".replace('a', "oo")         // => "boonoonoo" — element out, run in

members.name: reverse
members.summary: Reverse the order of the elements.

doc.code: "abc".reverse()              // => "cba"

members.name: runes
members.summary: Re-represent the text as `runes`, the O(1)-indexing form.

doc.code: "abc".runes()        // => u"abc" — the O(1)-indexing form

doc.markdown:
The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

members.name: slice
members.summary: Answer the symbols from `start` to `end`; bounds **clamp** (contrast `splice`, which raises), negative indices count from the end.

doc.markdown:
`slice` **clamps** out-of-range bounds (reading past the end is harmless); negative indices count from the
end. Equivalent to `s[start:end]` with a name usable in a chain; offsets are symbols.

doc.code:
"hello".slice(1, 3)          // => "el"
"hello".slice(3, 99)         // => "lo" — clamps
"hello".slice(-3, -1)        // => "ll"

members.name: snake_case
members.summary: Render the text as a `snake_case` identifier.

doc.markdown:
The four **identifier renderings** segment the text fully and normalise each word's interior. Word boundaries
are: runs of whitespace/`_`/`-` (discarded); a lower→upper transition; and in an upper run followed by a
lower, the last upper starts the new word (`parseXMLFile` → `parse` | `XML` | `File`). The boundary set is
closed — digits, apostrophes, and periods stay inside words:

doc.code:
"parseXMLFile".snake_case()      // => "parse_xml_file"
"Parse XML file".kebab_case()    // => "parse-xml-file"
"parse_xml_file".camel_case()    // => "parseXmlFile" — interior normalised
"parse xml file".pascal_case()   // => "ParseXmlFile"
"don't stop".snake_case()        // => "don't_stop" — the apostrophe is not a boundary

members.name: sort
members.summary: Order the symbols by code point; there is no comparator.

doc.code: "banana".sort()              // => "aaabnn"

members.name: splice
members.summary: Removes `delete_count` elements at `start`, then inserts the items there.

doc.markdown:
`splice` **raises** out of range (editing past the end is not harmless). Its inserts take the add-side
reading: runs spread, scalars are one element, anything else raises.

doc.code:
"abcd".splice(1, 2, "XY", 'z')  // => "aXYzd"
"ad".splice(1, 0, 'b')       // => "abd"
"ab".splice(5, 1)            // Error: index_out_of_bounds: 5 out of range [0, 2]

members.name: split
members.summary: Split the text into an array of the pieces between the separators.

doc.markdown:
Separators take the menu: element, run, homogeneous set, element-level predicate, or absent (the blank set).
**`split` has no limit argument.**

Two regimes, deliberately different:

- An **explicit separator** keeps empty pieces — n hits make n+1 pieces, so `"".split(",")` is `[""]`.
- The **no-argument form** yields the maximal runs of significant content — empties never appear, and
splitting pure filler yields `[]`.
- An empty-run separator matches nothing: `"ab".split("")` is `["ab"]`.

doc.code:
"a,b,,c".split(',')          // => ["a", "b", "", "c"] — empties kept
"a::b::c".split("::")        // => ["a", "b", "c"]
"a,b;c".split(',', ';')      // => ["a", "b", "c"] — separator set
"a1b2c".split(func(c) { return c >= '0' && c <= '9' })  // => ["a", "b", "c"]
"  a  b\tc ".split()         // => ["a", "b", "c"] — blank set, maximal runs
"   ".split()                // => []
"".split(",")                // => [""]

members.name: split_lines
members.summary: Split the text into an array of its lines at `\n`, `\r\n` or `\r`; a trailing line break adds no empty last line.

doc.code:
"a
b
c
".split_lines()  // => ["a", "b", "c"]

members.name: string
members.summary: Answer the receiver: a string is immutable and identity-less, so there is nothing to construct.

doc.markdown: The mutable-bodied types copy instead: see [`array()`](kavun:type/array/array).

members.name: time
members.summary: Parse the text as a `time` in the canonical grammar, as `time(text)` reads it; bad text raises unless a default is given.

doc.markdown: Any other spelling names its layout: see [`parse_time`](kavun:type/string/parse_time).

members.name: title_case
members.summary: Render the text as a label: each word's first symbol uppercased, the interior preserved.

doc.markdown:
`title_case()` is the **label rendering**: it segments on written boundaries only (whitespace/`_`/`-`),
uppercases each word's first symbol, and **preserves** the interior — a label keeps the author's emphasis:

doc.code:
"ATM fee".title_case()           // => "ATM Fee"
"iPhone".title_case()            // => "IPhone"
"hELLO world".title_case()       // => "HELLO World"
"atm_fee-total".title_case()     // => "Atm Fee Total"

members.name: trim
members.summary: Repeatedly drop the elements at both ends while they belong to the set (the blank set with no argument).

doc.markdown:
Strip **a set of elements**, repeating while they match. A run argument raises — the anchored-run form is
`remove_prefix`/`remove_suffix`. No argument trims the [blank set](kavun:type/string#the-blank-set).

doc.code:
"  hi  ".trim()                     // => "hi"
"xxhixy".trim('x', 'y')             // => "hi"
"abhiab".trim("ab")                 // Error: invalid_argument_type: trim takes elements — spell trim('a', 'b')

members.name: trim_end
members.summary: Drop the trailing elements that belong to the set (the blank set with no argument); see [`trim`](kavun:type/string/trim).

members.name: trim_start
members.summary: Drop the leading elements that belong to the set (the blank set with no argument); see [`trim`](kavun:type/string/trim).

members.name: unique
members.summary: Drop repeats, keeping each element at its first occurrence.

doc.code: "aabbaa".unique()            // => "ab"

members.name: upper
members.summary: Map every symbol to uppercase; see [`lower`](kavun:type/string/lower).

types.name: time
types.summary: An instant in time, with nanosecond precision and a time zone.

doc.markdown:
## Overview

`time` is a domain scalar: an absolute instant plus the zone it is *viewed* in. The zone affects the
calendar accessors (`hour()`, `day()`, …), calendar arithmetic and the rendered text; it never affects
identity — two values of the same instant in different zones are equal, and ordering and duration
arithmetic work on the instant.

Key rules, each expanded below:

- Next to a `time`, a bare `int` **operand** is a duration in **nanoseconds**; a bare `int` in a
**conversion** is a unix timestamp. Operator = duration, conversion = timestamp — and an int is a duration
wherever its member says so (`30.seconds()`, `d.in_hours()`).
- `time` and `int` deliberately do **not** compare: an instant and a bare number have no common order.
- **One strict text grammar** (below) for `t"…"`, `time(s)` and the canonical layouts — nothing is guessed.
Any other text shape names its **layout**: `time(s, layout)`, `s.parse_time(layout[, default])`.
- **A wall clock that does not name exactly one instant raises** — a time a daylight-saving gap skips, or one
an overlap repeats — whether it is constructed or computed. Nothing normalizes.
- A zone is an IANA name (`"Europe/Kyiv"`) or `"UTC"`. The host's own zone is never visible: `"Local"` and
`""` are not zone names, and `clock.now()` answers in UTC.
- One render surface: `format(spec)` with the format mini-language. One canonical text form: RFC3339 with
the fraction the instant carries (RFC3339Nano), used by `.string()`, f-strings, and the default
`format()`.

`time` values are immutable. The range is years 1…9999.

The calendar accessors are all zero-argument, answered in the value's own zone.

## Construction

### Text: the canonical grammar

`t"…"` literals, `time(s)` and the layouts `iso`/`isonano`/`date`/`datetime` read exactly this grammar:

| form | reads as |
| --- | --- |
| `YYYY-MM-DD` | midnight UTC |
| `YYYY-MM-DD` + `T` **or a space** + `HH:MM[:SS[.f]]` (1–9 fraction digits) | that wall clock, UTC |
| any of the above + `Z` / `±HH:MM` / `±HHMM` | that wall clock at the stated offset (`Z` and `+00:00` are UTC) |

Every field is fixed width and every value must exist. These raise `conversion` (a `t"…"` literal that does not
match is a compile error): unpadded fields (`"2026-8-9"`), slashes (`"12/01/2026"`), month names and free text,
bare digits (`"20260829"`, `"1700000000"` — name the unit with a layout), lowercase `t`/`z`, and impossible
values (`"2026-02-30"`, `"2026-08-29T24:00"`).

doc.code:
time("12/01/2026")                  // Error: conversion: cannot convert string to time: expected a 4-digit year at offset 0
time("2026-02-30")                  // Error: conversion: ...: day 30 out of range 1..28

doc.markdown:
### Text: layouts

Any other shape names its layout. On a text receiver the conversion member `s.time([default])` reads the
canonical grammar, like `time(s)`; reading under a layout is its own member, `s.parse_time(layout[, default])`,
whose default comes after the layout — so a layout can never be mistaken for a default:

doc.code:
time("29/08/2026", "%d/%m/%Y")              // free form: the second argument is the layout
"29/08/2026".parse_time("%d/%m/%Y")         // member form: the layout is required
"bad".parse_time("%d/%m/%Y", undefined)     // => undefined — the default, after the layout
"2026-08-29".parse_time("iso")              // the canonical grammar, spelled explicitly
"2026-08-29".time()                         // the canonical grammar: the conversion member
time("29/08/2026 03:04 PM", "%d/%m/%Y %I:%M %p")   // => time("2026-08-29T15:04:00Z")
time("1700000000", "unix")                  // => time("2023-11-14T22:13:20Z") — the layout names the unit

doc.markdown:
| layout | reads |
| --- | --- |
| `iso`, `isonano`, `date`, `datetime` | the canonical grammar above |
| `unix`, `unixms`, `unixmicro`, `unixnano` | an integer, in exactly that unit |
| `time`, `rfc822` | refused — no date / a 2-digit year and a zone abbreviation |
| a `%`-template (anything containing `%`) | the directives below; every other byte matches literally |

Readable directives — the inverse of the render directives, over the ones that read back unambiguously:
`%Y %m %d %e %j %H %I %M %S %f %p %P %z %s` (fixed width, exactly as rendered), `%B %b %A %a` (English
names, exact case; a weekday that contradicts the date raises), `%n %t %%`. Refused on input: `%y` (a century
pivot is a guess), `%Z` (an abbreviation names several zones), and the week-based `%G %V %u %w %C`. Unset fields
default to the zero value's (`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`). `%I` needs `%p`; `%s` stands alone.

A wrong **layout** is a mistake in the script, not a miss in the data, so it raises `invalid_value` even when a
default is given:

doc.code:
"x".parse_time("%y", undefined)           // Error: invalid_value — parse_time) directive %y cannot be parsed (ambiguous on input
"x".parse_time("%d/%m/%Y", undefined)     // => undefined — the data missed, the layout is fine

doc.markdown:
### Component records

A `dict` or `record` converts through the **components** reading — the same shape `components()` answers.
Every key is optional and defaults to the zero value's part; an unknown key raises; nothing normalizes:

doc.code:
time({year: 2026, month: 8, day: 29})                       // => time("2026-08-29T00:00:00Z")
time({year: 2026, month: 3, day: 29, hour: 15, zone: "Europe/Kyiv"})   // => time("2026-03-29T15:00:00+03:00")
time({year: 2026, hour: 1, zone_offset: 3600})              // => time("2026-01-01T01:00:00+01:00") — a fixed offset
time({})                                                    // => time("1970-01-01T00:00:00Z") — the zero time
time({yr: 2026})                                            // Error: invalid_value: (time) unknown component "yr"
time({year: 2026, month: 1, day: 32})                       // Error: invalid_value: (time) day 32 out of range 1..31

doc.markdown: `zone` makes the parts a wall clock in that zone, and the **one-instant rule** applies:

`zone` and `zone_offset` together must agree; `"Local"`, `""` and unknown names raise.

### Numbers

An `int` in conversion position is a **unix timestamp**; the member name picks the encoding:
`float` and `decimal` read as fractional unix seconds:

Every numeric conversion answers in **UTC** — an integer timestamp is host-independent, so its wall-clock
reading must be too.

### The free constructor and the clock

doc.code:
time()                     // => time("1970-01-01T00:00:00Z") — the zero time, unix 0
time(1700000000)           // ≡ (1700000000).time()
time("2026-08-29")         // the canonical grammar
time("29/08/2026", "%d/%m/%Y") // a layout (the free form has no default slot; the member does)
undefined.time(time())     // => time("1970-01-01T00:00:00Z") — the maybe-missing form

clock := import("clock")
clock.now()                                     // the current instant, in UTC (the clock module needs a grant)
1700000000.time() + 500                         // => time("2023-11-14T22:13:20.0000005Z") — seconds, then ns

doc.markdown:
On bad input every constructor **raises** a catchable error — none answers an `error` value. The current instant
is the only world read: it comes from the [`clock`](kavun:module/clock) module (`now`, `since`, `until`,
`sleep`). Calendar facts are members (`t.is_leap_year()`, `t.days_in_month()`).

## Operators

| expression | result | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `t + n` / `n + t` | `time` | `n` is a duration in **nanoseconds** |
| `t - n` | `time` | back by `n` nanoseconds |
| `t2 - t1` | `int` | the elapsed nanoseconds |
| `t1 < t2` (`<=` `>` `>=`) | `bool` | ordering of instants |
| `t == x` / `t != x` | `bool` | instant equality; `false`/`true` against any non-time |
| `n - t` | raises | an int minus an instant has no meaning |
| `t < n` / `n < t` | raises | deliberate — see below |
| `t + t2`, `t * n`, … | raises | no instant+instant, no scaling |

A duration is exact elapsed time; to move by **calendar** days or months, use the arithmetic members below.

### Reading a duration

A duration is nothing special — a plain `int` of nanoseconds. Its members read it in a unit, render it, and
build one (see [int § Durations](kavun:type/int#durations)):

doc.code:
t := t"2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
t2 := t"2026-08-29T16:04:05.123456789Z"
elapsed := t2 - t                  // => 3600000000000
elapsed / 1.minutes()              // => 60 — int division
elapsed.in_seconds()               // => 3600.0 — seconds, as a float
elapsed.in_minutes()               // => 60.0
elapsed.in_hours()                 // => 1.0
elapsed.duration_string()          // => "1h0m0s"
"1h".nanoseconds() == elapsed      // => true — the text form of the same reading

doc.markdown:
### The missing comparisons

**`time` vs `int` comparison is deliberately absent** — an instant and a bare number have no common order
(nanoseconds since when? seconds or millis?), so both directions raise instead of guessing:

doc.code:
t := t"2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
t < 1700000000            // Error: invalid_binary_operator: time < int
1700000000 < t            // Error: invalid_binary_operator: int < time
t == 1788015845           // => false — equality just answers "not the same value"

doc.markdown: Equality and ordering are zone-insensitive — they compare instants:

doc.code:
t := t"2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
kyiv := t.in_zone("Europe/Kyiv")
kyiv == t                 // => true — same instant, different view

doc.markdown:
## Conversions out

Every conversion is `x.T([default])`. An instant **as a number is its unix timestamp** — `int()` is a
deliberate synonym of `unix()` (the type name answers "as a number", the unit name "in which unit"). Each
conversion's own entry shows it.

There is deliberately no `bool()` (truthiness is `!!t` / `t.is_true()`), no `byte()`/`rune()`/`bytes()`
(no octet meaning), and no container targets or `len()` — an instant has no elements.

## Zone data

Zone names resolve through the host's IANA tzdata (Go's lookup order: `ZONEINFO`, the system copy,
`$GOROOT/lib/time/zoneinfo.zip`, and the embedded copy the `kavun` CLI links in). Zone rules change, so a
named-zone result can differ between hosts with different tzdata versions; UTC and fixed offsets never do.
See [embedding](kavun:doc/embedding#time-zone-data) for pinning tzdata and replaying past results.

members.name: add_days
members.summary: Move by `n` calendar days in the value's own zone, keeping the wall clock; see [`add_months`](kavun:type/time/add_months).

members.name: add_months
members.summary: Move by `n` calendar months in the value's own zone, keeping the wall clock, with the end-of-month `rule`.

doc.markdown:
`add_days`, `add_months` and `add_years` move the **calendar** day in the value's own zone and keep the wall
clock. The end-of-month rule is required — `"clamp"` or `"last_day"`, with no default — and only matters when
the start is a month end:

The kept wall clock follows the one-instant rule: landing in a daylight-saving gap or overlap **raises**.
UTC and fixed-offset times never do, so moving the arithmetic there is the explicit escape:

doc.code:
a := time({year: 2026, month: 3, day: 28, hour: 3, minute: 30, zone: "Europe/Kyiv"})
a.add_days(1)          // Error: invalid_value: 2026-03-29 03:30:00 does not exist in zone Europe/Kyiv (a daylight-saving gap)
a.add_days(2)          // => time("2026-03-30T03:30:00+03:00")
a.utc().add_days(1)    // => time("2026-03-29T01:30:00Z") — exactly 24h later, in UTC

members.name: add_years
members.summary: Move by `n` calendar years in the value's own zone, keeping the wall clock, with the end-of-month `rule`; see [`add_months`](kavun:type/time/add_months).

members.name: array
members.summary: Answer a new one-element `array` holding the receiver.

doc.markdown: Total, so the default is never used.

members.name: components
members.summary: Answer a record of the parts the instant can be rebuilt from.

doc.markdown:
Answers a record of exactly the parts the instant can be rebuilt from; the computed accessors
(`week_day`, `month_name`, `zone_name`) stay their own members. A value viewed in a named zone also carries
`zone`; UTC and fixed offsets are fully described by `zone_offset`:

doc.code:
t := t"2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
kyiv := t.in_zone("Europe/Kyiv")
t.components()
// {"year": 2026, "month": 8, "day": 29, "hour": 15, "minute": 4,
//  "second": 5, "nanosecond": 123456789, "zone_offset": 0}   (key order not significant)
kyiv.components().zone               // => "Europe/Kyiv"

time(t.components()) == t            // => true — the way back
dict(kyiv.components()).time() == kyiv   // => true — the conversion spelling, zone included

members.name: copy
members.summary: Answer the receiver — a `time` is always immutable.

doc.markdown: Identity no-ops on an immutable scalar — kept so generic code never type-errors:

members.name: date
members.summary: Answer the civil day in the value's own zone; see [`date_in`](kavun:type/time/date_in).

doc.code:
t := t"2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
t.date()                   // => date("2026-08-29") — the civil day in t's zone (see "To a date")

members.name: date_in
members.summary: Answer the civil day the instant falls on in the named zone.

doc.markdown:
A [`date`](kavun:type/date) is a civil day with no zone, so the conversion reads the day in a zone — the time's own, or
a named one:

doc.code:
t := t"2026-03-31T23:30:00Z"
t.date()                       // => date("2026-03-31") — the civil day in the time's own zone; ≡ date(t)
t.date_in("Europe/Kyiv")       // => date("2026-04-01") — the same instant is already April 1st in Kyiv

doc.markdown:
Near midnight the UTC day and the local day differ — name the zone the business day belongs to. The way back
is `d.time()` (midnight UTC) or `d.time_in(zone)` (the first instant of the day there).

members.name: day
members.summary: Answer the day of the month.

members.name: days_in_month
members.summary: Answer the number of days in the month.

members.name: days_in_year
members.summary: Answer the number of days in the year.

members.name: decimal
members.summary: Answer the unix timestamp in fractional seconds, exact to the nanosecond.

members.name: float
members.summary: Answer the unix timestamp in fractional seconds, approximate.

doc.code:
t := t"2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
t.float()                  // => 1788015845.1234567 — fractional seconds, approximate (~100ns today)

members.name: format
members.summary: Render the value per the [format mini-language](kavun:doc/format_mini_language).

doc.markdown:
`format` with the [format mini-language](kavun:doc/format_mini_language) is the *only* member that renders a
`time` — there is no `iso()`/`date()`/`format_date()` family. `#`-specs name the layouts; anything after
`#` that is not a named layout is a strftime-style pattern:

doc.code:
t := t"2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
t.format()                  // => "2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z" — RFC3339, precision-preserving
t.format("#iso")            // => "2026-08-29T15:04:05Z" — the explicitly seconds-truncating spec
t.format("#isonano")        // => "2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
t.format("#date")           // => "2026-08-29"
t.format("#time")           // => "15:04:05"
t.format("#datetime")       // => "2026-08-29 15:04:05"
t.format("#unix")           // => "1788015845" — #unixms, #unixmicro, #unixnano likewise
t.format("#rfc822")         // => "29 Aug 26 15:04 UTC"
t.format("#%d.%m.%Y %H:%M") // => "29.08.2026 15:04" — strftime directives
t.format("#%A, %B %e")      // => "Saturday, August 29"
t.format("#%I:%M %p")       // => "03:04 PM"

doc.markdown:
Supported strftime directives: `%Y %y %C %m %d %e %H %I %M %S %p %P %B %b %A %a %u %w %V %G %j %s %f
%Z %z %n %t %%` — an unknown directive raises. The same names read back as layouts (see
[Text: layouts](kavun:type/time#text-layouts) for which do).

members.name: freeze
members.summary: Answer the receiver — a `time` is always immutable; see [`copy`](kavun:type/time/copy).

members.name: hour
members.summary: Answer the hour, 0–23.

members.name: in_zone
members.summary: Answer the same instant viewed in the named zone.

doc.code:
kyiv := t"2026-08-29T12:04:05Z".in_zone("Europe/Kyiv")

kyiv                  // => time("2026-08-29T15:04:05+03:00") — same instant, viewed in Kyiv
kyiv.zone_name()      // => "EEST"
kyiv.zone_offset()    // => 10800 — seconds east of UTC
kyiv.utc()            // => time("2026-08-29T12:04:05Z") — same instant, viewed in UTC
kyiv.utc().hour()     // => 12
kyiv.in_zone("")      // Error: invalid_value: (in_zone) a zone name is required

doc.markdown:
`in_zone(name)`/`utc()` move the *view*, never the instant. Zone survives arithmetic: `(kyiv + n)` and
`kyiv.add_days(n)` keep the Kyiv view.

members.name: int
members.summary: Answer the unix timestamp in seconds, floored — a synonym of `unix()`.

members.name: is_leap_year
members.summary: Report whether the year is a leap year.

members.name: is_true
members.summary: Report truthiness: the zero time, the unix epoch, is falsy (`!!x` ⟺ `x != time()`).

doc.markdown:
Derived like every type's: a time is falsy exactly when it is the zero value `time()`, the unix epoch
`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` (in any zone). Every other instant is truthy — including `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, the
"unset" sentinel some backends (.NET's `default(DateTime)`) send. A host that means "missing" by such a
sentinel should map it to `undefined` before it reaches a script.

doc.code:
time().is_true()                       // => false — the zero time
(0).time().is_true()                   // => false — the same instant
t"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z".is_true()      // => true — a real instant
!time()                                // => true

members.name: minute
members.summary: Answer the minute, 0–59.

members.name: month
members.summary: Answer the month, 1–12 (January is 1).

members.name: month_name
members.summary: Answer the month's English name.

members.name: nanosecond
members.summary: Answer the nanosecond within the second.

members.name: runes
members.summary: Answer the one text form as `runes`; see [`string`](kavun:type/time/string).

members.name: second
members.summary: Answer the second, 0–59.

members.name: string
members.summary: Answer the one text form, RFC3339 with the fraction the instant carries.

doc.code:
t := t"2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z"
t.string()                 // => "2026-08-29T15:04:05.123456789Z" — the ONE text form, RFC3339Nano
time(t.string()) == t      // => true — the text form round-trips through the canonical grammar

doc.markdown:
The `default` is taken for interface uniformity — every conversion carries it — and is never used: the
conversion is total.

members.name: time
members.summary: Answer the receiver, the identity conversion.

members.name: unix
members.summary: Answer the seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, floored.

doc.markdown:
Every integral reading **floors** — the containing interval is the meaning, not a discarded remainder, so
half a second *before* the epoch is second `-1`, not `0`:

doc.code:
tn := 0.time() - 500.milliseconds()   // 0.5s before the epoch
tn.unix()                              // => -1
tn.unix_ms()                           // => -500

members.name: unix_micro
members.summary: Answer the microseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, floored; see [`unix`](kavun:type/time/unix).

members.name: unix_ms
members.summary: Answer the milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, floored; see [`unix`](kavun:type/time/unix).

members.name: unix_nano
members.summary: Answer the nanoseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, floored; see [`unix`](kavun:type/time/unix).

members.name: utc
